A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe CLIMP, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Much of v1 Appendix A can be matched to v2's main text. However, v2 references supplementary material absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of detailed benchmark results and its new ResNet evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, robustness, resolution-scaling, embedding-geometry, and ablation results, including detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original CLIMP experiments and adds reported MetaCLIP, Qwen2, Hydra, and ResNet comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed VMamba vision encoder, Mamba-1/Mamba-2 text encoders, last-token pooling, learned projections, and contrastive dual-encoder architecture remain unchanged. Additional encoders appear as experimental comparators, not revisions to CLIMP.

E1.justification: The explicitly identified evaluation datasets and tasks are retained. v2 additionally reports a ResNet comparison on 38 OpenCLIP benchmarks, but does not identify those benchmarks in the supplied material. The increased count alone cannot establish which data populations or task requirements were added.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparisons: Table 1 adds MetaCLIP-ViT-B/16; Table 10 adds RoPE-ViT with Qwen2-1.5B and VMamba with bidirectional Hydra; Section 4.1 reports comparisons against convolutional ResNet-based CLIP models. Exact ResNet variants are deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

E3.justification: The added MetaCLIP comparator uses vision weights pretrained on MetaCLIP-400M, introducing a different pretraining condition. The text-encoder ablation adds model configurations including Qwen2-1.5B. Existing CC12M training budgets, optimization settings, resolutions, and metrics remain unchanged; the full-caption clarification does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 extends v1 Table 8 with Qwen2 and Hydra, expanding the text-backbone ablation to another Transformer LLM and a bidirectional SSM. Existing spatial-shuffling, geometry, scaling, and qualitative analyses are retained across relocation. The new discussion of architectural failure conditions does not document additional robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both present point estimates and plots without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds MetaCLIP scores of 25.7/56.9 Acc@1/5 and 66.4/76.2 IR/TR@5, Qwen2 and Hydra result rows, and a reported greater-than-four-point average advantage over ResNets. MetaCLIP's image recall exceeds CLIMP's 65.5 under different pretraining. Extensive per-dataset results from v1 Appendix Tables 9-10 are absent from the supplied v2, while matched retained numerical tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The continuous and discrete SSM equations, last-token pooling definition, and scalar-transition decay argument are retained. Added intuitive explanations and discussion of Mamba variants introduce no new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central fully Mamba-based architecture, retrieval, robustness, and resolution-flexibility claims remain. v2 adds scaling as an explicit abstract, introduction, and conclusion contribution, strengthening the assertion that architectural advantages should persist beyond the tested training regime.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for Mamba-1 versus Mamba-2 performance and Hydra's results, acknowledges NaFlex's DOCCI text-retrieval and image-geometry strengths, and discusses potential Transformer advantages for low resolution and visual-style shifts. It also removes v1's explicit large-scale verification limitation and strengthens architectural-versus-data-scale interpretations despite retaining the original scaling evidence.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public code-and-model availability statement with repository access information. Section 4.4 newly clarifies that every comparator processes complete captions and states the LLaMA baseline's 8K context. The dense-caption image resolutions were already disclosed in v1's appendix; their main-text appearance is relocation.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit positioning against LLM2CLIP and UniViTAR, clarifies its distinction from hybrid CLIP-Mamba architectures, and adds discussion and citations concerning SSM length extrapolation, caption adaptation, and interpretability. These extend the context while preserving the central fully SSM-based novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the abstract, contribution list, and experimental discussion, integrates much of Appendix A into the main narrative, and replaces numbered analysis subsections with run-in headings. The separate Limitations section disappears, an Acknowledgments section is added, and citations change from author-year to numerical style.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout with widespread resizing and relocation. v1 Appendix Tables 11-14 become v2 Tables 4-7, and v1 Figures 2 and 5 merge into v2 Figure 2. Summary displays are replaced by existing detailed tables, comparator rows are added, and v1 Tables 9-10 and Figure 6 are absent.

improvement.justification: Added comparators, clearer full-caption evaluation, code-access information, and the corrected qualification of DOCCI performance improve transparency. However, detailed benchmark breakdowns are unavailable in v2, and stronger scaling claims replace an explicit limitation. Section 4.5 claims an advantage across all data sizes although the retained Figure 4 shows RoPE-ViT ahead at 1M and 3M. These benefits and losses, together with the missing referenced supplement, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
